definitions.gloss: final stage, terminal phase, end period
definitions.explanation: The last stage or closing period of something, whether a historical era, a process, or a disease. Often implies decline or approaching end.

examples.japanese: {江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}の{末期|まっき}に{開国|かいこく}した。
examples.english: Japan opened its borders in the final period of the Edo era.

examples.japanese: {末期|まっき}がんと{診断|しんだん}された。
examples.english: He was diagnosed with terminal cancer.

examples.japanese: ローマ{帝国|ていこく}の{末期|まっき}は{政治|せいじ}が{混乱|こんらん}していた。
examples.english: Politics were in turmoil in the final period of the Roman Empire.

notes:
USAGE:
Used as a noun modifier: {末期|まっき}の or as a prefix: {末期|まっき}がん (terminal cancer). Very common in both historical contexts (the final period of an era) and medical contexts (terminal stage of a disease). Also read as まつご in the compound {末期|まつご}の{水|みず} (water given to a dying person).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {末期|まっき}がん: terminal cancer
- {末期|まっき}{症状|しょうじょう}: terminal symptoms
- ～{時代|じだい}の{末期|まっき}: final period of the ~ era
- {末期|まっき}{的|てき}: end-stage, decadent
